Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll begin with `README.md`, then use the required `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect the current multi-wake keyframes before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and produce one candidate plus both required documentation updates.

The baseline guidance confirms the seed’s dominant failure: strong lateral escape with little upstream progress, so propulsion-only retuning is already a falsified direction. I’m now comparing all four sampled rollouts—including inherited optimizer notes—before choosing the single feedback change.

The visual comparison sharpens the failure mode: the high-progress policy actively moves upstream but folds during an unchecked turn; the prefilled guarded descendant stays finite and below the hard acceleration cap, yet curls into a large loop and exits upward with negative progress. I’m checking the exposed state conventions now so the candidate can isolate course damping without inventing unavailable signals.

The inherited results rule out two tempting “safe” fixes: phase-radius regulation was almost pure advection, and the slower 15° angle-only/yaw-damped candidate exited downstream in 10.02 units. The surviving hypothesis is narrower: hold the prefilled gait and safety guards fixed, but replace its effectively bang-bang bearing curvature with a graded bearing-plus-yaw command to stop the observed closed turn. I’m recording that diagnosis before editing, as the visual-evidence skill requires.

Both required provenance files are now updated, and the single candidate changes only the course map plus its owned damping parameter. The durable lesson records the key negative boundary: lowering loads or extending survival did not help when the trajectory became advective or looped. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated checker next.

The first mandated check exposed a pre-existing workspace-rendering defect before evaluating my edits: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, while the checker requires exactly one marker. I’m inspecting the checker and duplicate lines to determine whether this can be resolved without modifying any read-only workspace surface.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated parent marker. The Julia contract command itself cannot start because this runner image has no `julia` on `PATH`; I’m checking the standard local install locations before treating that as an environment limitation. No CFD is being run.

All three mandated checks now pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy materialization/finite output, and repository boundary/schema validation. I used the workspace’s bundled Julia executable after confirming the default `PATH` omission. I’m doing a final audit of the exact candidate and documentation deltas; no CFD rollout will be started.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate in [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1). It preserves the guarded gait while replacing persistently saturated bearing steering with graded bearing-plus-turn-rate damping.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:35)

All mandated checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/finite output, and solver boundary/schema validation. I also removed an exact duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the checker from running. No CFD was run.
